title: Majorana bilinears, compact modular seeds and the approach to the Tsirelson bound
authors: M. S. Guimaraes, I. Roditi, S. P. Sorella
abstract: In this work we study the Bell-CHSH inequality in the vacuum of the free massive Majorana field in $1+1$ dimensions, taking as the dichotomic observables of the two parties even bilinears of smeared fields localized in the right and in the left Rindler wedges. The test functions are generated from seeds in the modular-frequency variable through the Tomita-Takesaki operator of the right wedge and, on the side of the left wedge, through its adjoint multiplied by $i$, which accounts for twisted duality. For seeds supported at positive modular frequency the one-particle overlaps between the two parties do not depend on the modular weights, and we obtain the Bell parameter in closed form. When the seeds are phase rotations of a single compact bump, the bilinears generate a copy of the Pauli algebra in each wedge, and we compute exactly the correlation matrix of the vacuum restricted to the two copies. The optimal settings violate the classical bound up to spectral widths more than twice as large as those reached with planar settings. We also show that the Tsirelson bound is never attained in the wedge vacuum for any choice of dichotomic observables, and that approaching it forces the modular spectral weight of the Bell vectors to concentrate at the spectral point $λ=1$ of the modular operator. This establishes in a precise way how the even sector of the free Majorana field realizes the Summers-Werner mechanism.
summary: This work studies Bell-CHSH violations in the vacuum of a 1+1 dimensional Majorana field using modular theory. The authors show that while the correlations violate classical bounds, the Tsirelson bound is never reached in the wedge vacuum. The study precisely maps how the field's even sector realizes the Summers-Werner mechanism by constraining the spectral weight near the bound.
main_problem: The paper investigates the violation of the Bell-CHSH inequality using vacuum states of a free massive Majorana field in 1+1 dimensions, specifically determining how close the correlations can approach the Tsirelson bound.
main_result: The Tsirelson bound is shown to be unattainable in the wedge vacuum, and approaching it forces the modular spectral weight of the Bell vectors to concentrate at the spectral point $\lambda=1$.
method: The analysis employs techniques from algebraic quantum field theory, utilizing the modular-frequency representation and the Tomita-Takesaki theory to calculate correlation functions for localized observables (bilinears).
model_or_system: The system is a free massive Majorana field in $1+1$ dimensions, whose vacuum state is analyzed by restricting observables to localized regions (Rindler wedges).
key_observables: The Bell-CHSH parameter, one-particle overlaps, and the modular spectral weight of the Bell vectors.
important_parameters: The modular frequency variable ($\omega$), the width parameter ($\sigma$), and the separation distance ($d$) between localized regions.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the vacuum state within Rindler wedges where the Bisognano-Wichmann theorem applies, and it does not cover correlations at finite distance.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the deficit ($2\sqrt{2} - 	ext{BCHSH}$) decreasing quadratically with the width parameter $\sigma$ for a fixed number of modes ($N=6$), confirming the approach to the bound.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the observables using modular theory, calculating the correlation matrix for specific seed configurations (like phase rotations of a single bump), deriving the Bell parameter in closed form, and finally performing numerical optimization to study the approach to the Tsirelson bound.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, physical realization (Majorana vacuum) where fundamental quantum information bounds (Tsirelson) are tested against algebraic constraints derived from quantum field theory (modular theory).
